ruleName: Ball moves after being put back
group: Ball moves after being put back
title: What happens if the ball rolls away after being replaced?
question: After you have marked, lifted, and replaced your ball on the green, it suddenly rolls away on its own before you take your putt. What should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position
Replace the ball on its original spot with no penalty
Take a penalty stroke and put it back
Start the hole over from the tee

explanation: If the ball moves on its own after being replaced, you must put it back on its original spot with no penalty.
imagePrompt: A teenage girl kneeling on the green, watching in surprise as her ball gently rolls away after she has already replaced it and isn't near it.
imageAlt: Teen girl golfer on green, watching her replaced ball roll away before putting.

issues: The golfer is shown kneeling rather than standing, but this aligns with the prompt intent for kneeling observation.
The clothing (orange top, blue shorts), skin tone, and hat are accurate; putting green and putter are realistic.
Only one golf ball is visible with correct size and perspective.
Putter is full-length, realistic with a proper club head.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the teenage girl is kneeling farther back from the ball to accentuate 'not near the ball' and very clearly observing it roll away. Maintain all other details.
